IDS.name: equilibrium
IDS.documentation: Description of a 2D, axi-symmetric, tokamak equilibrium; result of an equilibrium code.

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.name: occurrence_type
field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.name: data_dictionary
field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer
field.documentation: Version of Access Layer used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: plugins
field.documentation: Information about the plugins used to write/read this IDS. This structure is filled automatically by the Access Layer at GET/PUT time, no need to fill it via a user program.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which a plugin has been applied

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the plugin applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: put_operation
field.documentation: Plugins used to PUT a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, if so they are listed by order of application)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: readback
field.documentation: Plugins to be used to read back a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, listed in reverse order of application)

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: library
field.documentation: List of external libraries used by the code that has produced this IDS

field.name: description
field.documentation: Short description of the software (type, purpose)

field.name: parameters
field.documentation: List of the code specific parameters in XML format

field.name: get_operation
field.documentation: Plugins actually used to read back a node (potentially, multiple plugins can be applied, listed in reverse order of application). This information is filled by the plugin infrastructure during the GET operation.

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means counter-clockwise when viewed from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: grids_ggd
field.documentation: Grids (using the Generic Grid Description), for various time slices. The timebase of this array of structure must be a subset of the time_slice timebase

field.name: grid
field.documentation: Set of GGD grids for describing the equilibrium, at a given time slice

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: time_slice
field.documentation: Set of equilibria at various time slices

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Description of the plasma boundary. The boundary can be either the real separatrix (provided by a free boundary equilibrium solver) or the 0.99x psi_norm flux surface provided by a fixed boundary equilibrium

field.name: outline
field.documentation: RZ outline of the plasma boundary

field.name: psi_norm
field.documentation: Value of the normalized poloidal flux at which the boundary is taken, the flux being normalized to its value at the separatrix (so psi_norm = 1 if the boundary is the separatrix)

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal flux at which the boundary is taken. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: geometric_axis
field.documentation: RZ position of the geometric axis (defined as (Rmin+Rmax) / 2 and (Zmin+Zmax) / 2 of the boundary)

field.name: minor_radius
field.documentation: Minor radius of the plasma boundary (defined as (Rmax-Rmin) / 2 of the boundary)

field.name: triangularity_upper
field.documentation: Upper triangularity of the plasma boundary

field.name: triangularity_lower
field.documentation: Lower triangularity of the plasma boundary

field.name: squareness_upper_inner
field.documentation: Upper inner squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_upper_outer
field.documentation: Upper outer squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_inner
field.documentation: Lower inner squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_outer
field.documentation: Lower outer squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: closest_wall_point
field.documentation: Position and distance to the plasma boundary of the point of the first wall which is the closest to plasma boundary

field.name: dr_dz_zero_point
field.documentation: Outboard point on the separatrix on which dr/dz = 0 (local maximum of the major radius of the separatrix). In case of multiple local maxima, the closest one from z=z_magnetic_axis is chosen.

field.name: gap
field.documentation: Set of gaps, defined by a reference point and a direction.

field.name: name
field.documentation: Short string identifier (unique for a given device)

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the reference point

field.name: angle
field.documentation: Angle measured clockwise from radial cylindrical vector (grad R) to gap vector (pointing away from reference point)

field.name: value
field.documentation: Value of the gap, i.e. distance between the reference point and the separatrix along the gap direction

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate at the selected plasma boundary

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal flux at the selected plasma boundary. Positive when the toroidal magnetic field is counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: phi_poloidal_current
field.documentation: Toroidal flux at the selected plasma boundary generated by the plasma poloidal current. Positive when the toroidal magnetic field is counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: contour_tree
field.documentation: Description of the topological connectivity of the poloidal flux map critical points as an undirected graph. Critical points are ether local extremum (o-points) or saddle points (x-points) of the poloidal flux map. X-points have zero gradients in orthogonal directions but are not local extremum of the poloidal flux map whilst O-points are.

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of nodes. A contour tree node is defined by its critical type and position within the poloidal plane. A critical type of 1 references an x-point whilst a critical type of 0 or 2 references an o-point. Both X-points and O-points are rarely coincident with nodes defining the poloidal upon which the poloidal flux map is defined. The order in which the critical points are stored in the nodes array of structure is only important for the primary plasma O-point and X-points. If present, the primary plasma O-point should be placed as the first element of the nodes array of structure. If present, the primary plasma X-point should be the second element in the nodes structure

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal flux at the node. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: levelset
field.documentation: Single poloidal flux contour including critical point (x-point only)

field.name: edges
field.documentation: Edges connect nodes to one another. A single node may connect to multiple edges such as the case where a single maximum (a hill) may topologically link to multiple minima (the floors of different valleys). For each edge (1st dimension), the index of the two connected nodes are listed (index referring to the ../node array)

field.name: constraints
field.documentation: In case of equilibrium reconstruction under constraints, measurements used to constrain the equilibrium, reconstructed values and accuracy of the fit. The names of the child nodes correspond to the following definition: the solver aims at minimizing a cost function defined as : J=1/2*sum_i [ weight_i^2 (reconstructed_i - measured_i)^2 / sigma_i^2 ]. in which sigma_i is the standard deviation of the measurement error (to be found in the IDS of the measurement)

field.name: b_field_tor_vacuum_r
field.documentation: Vacuum field times major radius in the toroidal field magnet. Positive sign means counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: source
field.documentation: Path to the source data for this measurement in the IMAS data dictionary

field.name: time_measurement
field.documentation: Exact time slice used from the time array of the measurement source data. If the time slice does not exist in the time array of the source data, it means linear interpolation has been used

field.name: exact
field.documentation: Integer flag : 1 means exact data, taken as an exact input without being fitted; 0 means the equilibrium code does a least square fit

field.name: sigma
field.documentation: Standard deviation of the measurement error

field.name: reconstructed
field.documentation: Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium

field.name: chi_squared
field.documentation: Squared error normalized by the variance considered in the minimization process : chi_squared = weight^2 *(reconstructed - measured)^2 / sigma^2, where sigma is the standard deviation of the measurement error

field.documentation: Sum of the chi_squared of all constraints used for the equilibrium reconstruction, divided by the number of degrees of freedom of the identification model

field.name: freedom_degrees_n
field.documentation: Number of degrees of freedom of the identification model

field.name: constraints_n
field.documentation: Number of constraints used (i.e. having a non-zero weight)

field.name: beta_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal beta. Defined as betap = 4 int(p dV) / [R_0 * mu_0 * Ip^2]

field.name: beta_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal beta, defined as the volume-averaged total perpendicular pressure divided by (B0^2/(2*mu0)), i.e. beta_toroidal = 2 mu0 int(p dV) / V / B0^2

field.name: beta_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal beta, defined as 100 * beta_tor * a[m] * B0 [T] / ip [MA]

field.name: ip
field.documentation: Plasma current (toroidal component). Positive sign means counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

field.name: area
field.documentation: Area of the LCFS poloidal cross section

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: length_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal length of the magnetic surface

field.name: psi_axis
field.documentation: Poloidal flux at the magnetic axis. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Poloidal flux at the magnetic axis. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Poloidal flux at the selected plasma boundary. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: rho_tor_boundary
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate at the selected plasma boundary

field.name: magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Magnetic axis position and toroidal field

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the magnetic axis

field.name: b_field_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis. Positive sign means counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: current_centre
field.documentation: Position and vertical velocity of the current centre

field.name: r
field.documentation: Major radius of the current center, defined as integral over the poloidal cross section of (j_tor*r*dS) / Ip

field.name: z
field.documentation: Height of the current center, defined as integral over the poloidal cross section of (j_tor*z*dS) / Ip

field.name: velocity_z
field.documentation: Vertical velocity of the current center

field.name: q_axis
field.documentation: q at the magnetic axis. Positive when toroidal current and toroidal magnetic field are in the same direction

field.name: q_95
field.documentation: q at the 95% poloidal flux surface (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: value
field.documentation: Minimum q value. Positive when toroidal current and toroidal magnetic field are in the same direction

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Minimum q position in normalized toroidal flux coordinate

field.name: psi_norm
field.documentation: Minimum q position in normalised poloidal flux

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Minimum q position in poloidal flux. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: energy_mhd
field.documentation: Plasma energy content = 3/2 * int(p,dV) with p being the total pressure (thermal + fast particles) [J]. Time-dependent; Scalar

field.name: psi_external_average
field.documentation: Average (over the plasma poloidal cross section) plasma poloidal magnetic flux produced by all external circuits (CS and PF coils, eddy currents, VS in-vessel coils), given by the following formula : int(psi_external.j_tor.dS) / Ip. For a positive plasma current (counter-clockwise when viewed from above), increases from the magnetic axis to the boundary

field.name: v_external
field.documentation: External voltage, i.e. time derivative of psi_external_average (with a minus sign : - d_psi_external_average/d_time)

field.name: plasma_inductance
field.documentation: Plasma inductance 2 E_magnetic/Ip^2, where E_magnetic = 1/2 * int(psi.j_tor.dS) (integral over the plasma poloidal cross-section)

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Equilibrium profiles (1D radial grid) as a function of the poloidal flux

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: phi
field.documentation: Toroidal flux. Positive when the toroidal magnetic field is counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: f
field.documentation: Diamagnetic function (F=R B_Phi). Positive when the toroidal field is counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: dpressure_dpsi
field.documentation: Derivative of pressure w.r.t. psi. Sign depends on the poloidal flux sign convention

field.name: f_df_dpsi
field.documentation: Derivative of F w.r.t. Psi, multiplied with F. Sign depends on the poloidal flux sign convention

field.name: j_phi
field.documentation: Flux surface averaged toroidal current density = average(j_tor/R) / average(1/R). Positive sign means counter-clockwise when viewed from above

field.name: j_parallel
field.documentation: Flux surface averaged approximation to parallel current density = average(j.B) / B0, where B0 = /vacuum_toroidal_field/b0. Sign is positive when the scalar product j.B is in the same direction as B0 (the signed vacuum toroidal field at R0)

field.name: q
field.documentation: Safety factor (only positive when toroidal current and magnetic field are in same direction)

field.name: magnetic_shear
field.documentation: Magnetic shear, defined as rho_tor/q . dq/drho_tor

field.name: r_inboard
field.documentation: Radial coordinate (major radius) on the inboard side of the magnetic axis

field.name: r_outboard
field.documentation: Radial coordinate (major radius) on the outboard side of the magnetic axis

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal flux, phi, corresponds to time_slice/profiles_1d/phi, the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation). Namely (rho_tor(rho)-rho_tor(magnetic_axis)) / (rho_tor(boundary)-rho_tor(magnetic_axis))

field.name: dpsi_drho_tor
field.documentation: Derivative of Psi with respect to Rho_Tor. Sign follows the poloidal flux convention

field.name: geometric_axis
field.documentation: RZ position of the geometric axis of the magnetic surfaces (defined as (Rmin+Rmax) / 2 and (Zmin+Zmax) / 2 of the surface)

field.name: squareness_upper_inner
field.documentation: Upper inner squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_upper_outer
field.documentation: Upper outer squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_inner
field.documentation: Lower inner squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: squareness_lower_outer
field.documentation: Lower outer squareness (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed in the flux surface

field.name: rho_volume_norm
field.documentation: Normalized square root of enclosed volume (radial coordinate). The normalizing value is the enclosed volume at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation)

field.name: dvolume_dpsi
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the volume enclosed in the flux surface with respect to Psi. Sign depends on the poloidal flux sign convention

field.name: dvolume_drho_tor
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the volume enclosed in the flux surface with respect to Rho_Tor

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: darea_dpsi
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the cross-sectional area of the flux surface with respect to psi. Sign depends on the poloidal flux sign convention

field.name: darea_drho_tor
field.documentation: Radial derivative of the cross-sectional area of the flux surface with respect to rho_tor

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: b_field_average
field.documentation: Flux surface averaged modulus of B (always positive, irrespective of the sign convention for the B-field direction).

field.name: b_field_min
field.documentation: Minimum(modulus(B)) on the flux surface (always positive, irrespective of the sign convention for the B-field direction)

field.name: b_field_max
field.documentation: Maximum(modulus(B)) on the flux surface (always positive, irrespective of the sign convention for the B-field direction)
